EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The past 24 hours saw significant escalation in regional tensions, with Iran warning it would target economic interests of states aiding the US economic war and potentially close the Strait of Hormuz if commitments are not met. Concurrently, Israel confirmed a strike in southern Syria against a "terror operative" posing an immediate threat, and Hamas accused Israel of ceasefire violations after an IDF strike in Gaza killed a company commander involved in tunnel reconstruction.

IRAN
Mohsen Rezai, Secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, stated that Iran would "certainly make changes in the management of the war," accusing Americans of betraying negotiations and commitments. He threatened to target the economic interests of any neighboring countries that assist the US economic war against Iran, explicitly stating that if this continues, "not a single drop of oil will exit the Persian Gulf and Strait of Hormuz." Rezai added that the Strait of Hormuz is "closed until the US fulfills commitments" and that Iran is ready to target all US oil and economic companies in the region. He also claimed that Trump's "stupidity" in attacking Iran has increased global enthusiasm for atomic bombs. Acting Defense Minister Brig. Gen. Seyyed Majid Ibn Al-Reza affirmed that Iran would never surrender to pressure, had kept defense production lines active during wartime, and had deployed new offensive and defensive systems. He warned that "new systems are ready; the battlefield will be the perfect place to test them." Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf stated that Tehran has received messages from neighboring countries about new security and economic arrangements in the region. First Vice President Mohammad Reza Aref vowed that the government would not allow US economic terrorism to target economic stability and livelihoods. Iraq's President stated that Iran did not request delays in the weapons disarmament file and confirmed Iran allows some Iraqi oil tankers to pass through the Strait of Hormuz. Satellite imagery reportedly showed fuel tanks in Abu Dhabi covered by metallic fences to prevent drone attacks, suggesting previous hits. An official at the Stars and Stripes newspaper was reportedly fired for stating he wouldn't censor news for soldiers, with the Pentagon sending notifications of dismissal.

ISRAEL
Israel confirmed an airstrike in southern Syria, targeting a "terror operative who advanced terror attacks in final stages of preparation" near Beit Jinn, stating the individual posed an immediate threat to forces. Syrian media reported one injured. The IDF also confirmed killing Sharif al-Hasanat, a Hamas company commander in the Deir al-Balah battalion in central Gaza, who was involved in restoring tunnels and advancing attacks. The IDF justified this strike during the ceasefire by stating Hasanat posed an immediate threat. Four incendiary kites from Gaza landed near Be'eri in the Gaza envelope; Sha'ar HaNegev Regional Council head Uri Epstein demanded immediate action and warned against a "it'll be fine" policy. Prime Minister Netanyahu declared that "as long as I am Prime Minister, a Palestinian state controlled by Iran will not be established: not in Gaza, and not in Judea and Samaria. Period." Foreign Minister Gideon Sa'ar criticized the "change government" as a failure and opposition leaders as "garden gnomes." Shin Bet decided not to provide security for Gadi Eisenkot, with his headquarters accusing the government of political motives. Defense Minister Katz responded to US envoy Tom Barrack's claims about political motivations for the Syria strike, stating the IDF recommended the strike based on clear intelligence about Turkey's intentions. Israel's Channel 12, citing the Foreign Minister, stated Israel prefers diplomatic solutions with Turkey. Israel informed Washington of its concern about Turkey deploying air defense systems at Abu al-Dhuhur airport in Syria.

GAZA & WEST BANK
The IDF killed Sharif al-Hasanat, a Hamas company commander in the Deir al-Balah battalion in central Gaza, who was involved in rebuilding underground infrastructure and advancing terror attacks. Hamas sources accused Israel of a ceasefire violation. Four incendiary kites from Gaza were found near Be'eri, prompting calls for immediate action from Sha'ar HaNegev Regional Council head Uri Epstein. In the West Bank, a fire engulfed hundreds of cars in Kiryat Arba, with 17 firefighting teams responding. An Israeli reportedly attacked an elderly Palestinian with a club in Judea, causing minor injuries; no arrests were made. Mansour Abbas, head of the Ra'am party, stated that "the state of Palestine exists and stands, and most countries in the world recognize it, except for the United States and Israel," and that Ra'am seeks recognition from these two countries. Netanyahu and Eisenkot both rejected the establishment of a Palestinian state.

LEBANON
Israeli forces launched a series of air and artillery attacks on southern Lebanon, targeting areas including Al-Mansouri, Wadi Srebbine, and Srobbin. Lebanese state media reported the use of phosphorus shells. Hezbollah's Deputy Political Council Head stated that Ansar Allah (Houthis) is ready to close the Bab el-Mandeb Strait if the "resistance" and its people in Lebanon face comprehensive pressure. Families of 11 journalists killed in Lebanon demanded that Israeli authorities be tried before the ICC for war crimes.

SYRIA & IRAQ
The IDF confirmed a strike in southern Syria against a terror operative advancing attacks near Beit Jinn, around 10 kilometers from the Israeli border, with Syrian media reporting one injury. Separately, Israeli forces reportedly conducted a new ground incursion into areas of Syria's Quneitra province and ransacked a house. An explosive device detonated in a bus belonging to the Al-Julani gangs on the Ma'rouneh-Saidnaya road in rural Damascus, injuring several people. Qatar condemned the Israeli attack on a civilian car in rural Damascus, calling it a dangerous and unacceptable provocation. Iraq's President stated that the international coalition came at Iraq's request to confront ISIS and is no longer needed, with its withdrawal set for September 30. Iraq's Communications Minister said the file of confining weapons to the state needs realism and deep discussion, not fixed deadlines. A Syrian citizen residing in Iraq was issued an arrest warrant for leading a gang and threatening Iraqis with Al-Julani gangs.

GULF STATES
Mohsen Rezai warned Gulf states against joining the US economic war, threatening to target their interests and ensure "not a single drop of oil will exit the Persian Gulf and Strait of Hormuz." Trump reiterated his stance that the Strait of Hormuz is "American territory." Axios reported that 40 tankers carried 16 million barrels of oil through the Strait of Hormuz on Friday night, a volume comparable to pre-crisis levels when considering Saudi and UAE alternative export routes. CNN claimed that Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Qatar, and the UAE are using tankers that turn off transponders and transfer oil in the Gulf of Oman, with US Navy assistance, to bypass high insurance risks and Iranian threats. Satellite images show metallic fences around fuel storage tanks at Dubai International Airport, reportedly to prevent drone strikes, with suggestions of previous hits. Iran demanded the immediate repatriation of three "severely injured and ill" Iranian pilots held in Qatar, stating their detention location on water is unsuitable and urging their transfer to land and a hospital. Kuwait was asked to facilitate initial contact between the pilots and their families. Saudi exports from Yanbu continue to decline, with only one VLCC being loaded and total refined products and crude oil exports likely below 4 million barrels per day, possibly due to Houthi attacks.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1. Mohsen Rezai, Secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, warned neighboring states against aiding the US economic war, threatening to target their interests and effectively close the Strait of Hormuz.
2. The IDF conducted an airstrike in southern Syria near Beit Jinn, targeting a "terror operative" who posed an immediate threat and was advancing terror attacks.
3. The IDF killed Sharif al-Hasanat, a Hamas company commander in the Deir al-Balah battalion, in central Gaza, citing his involvement in tunnel restoration and advancing terror attacks.
4. Four incendiary kites from Gaza crossed into Israel and were found near Be'eri, raising concerns about escalating threats from the Gaza envelope.
5. US envoy to Turkey, Tom Barrack, questioned Israel's motivations for the Syria strike, suggesting a possible attempt to "lure" Turkey into conflict or a breakdown in communication, while Defense Minister Katz dismissed political motives.
6. Donald Trump stated that he considers the Strait of Hormuz "American territory" and believes Iran is "desperate for a deal."
7. Iran demanded the immediate repatriation of three injured Iranian pilots held by Qatari forces, citing unsuitable conditions.
8. Iraq announced the full withdrawal of the US-led international coalition by September 30, deeming their presence no longer necessary for confronting ISIS.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
Escalation risks are high due to Iran's explicit threats to target economic interests of supporting states and potentially close the Strait of Hormuz, directly challenging US posture and regional stability. Israel's confirmed strikes in Gaza and Syria, targeting key operatives, maintain active flashpoints and demonstrate a willingness to act against immediate threats, potentially provoking further retaliation from Hamas and Syrian-aligned groups. The ongoing US-Iran economic warfare, characterized by sanctions and Iranian counter-threats regarding oil flow, presents a significant risk to global energy markets and maritime security in the Persian Gulf. The presence of incendiary kites from Gaza indicates persistent, albeit low-level, cross-border aggression that could escalate. Iran's acting Defense Minister's statements about new military systems being ready for "the battlefield" signal a potential for increased military engagement if red lines are crossed.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
**US:** President Trump reiterated that he considers the Strait of Hormuz "American territory" and views Iran as "desperate for a deal" due to economic pressure. He indicated that the US is observing developments with Iran's economic situation and maintains "complete control" over the Strait. US envoy to Turkey, Tom Barrack, questioned the timing and motives of an Israeli strike in Syria, suggesting it might be an attempt to "lure" Turkey into a conflict.
**Gulf States:** Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Qatar, and the UAE are reportedly using evasive measures, including turning off transponders and transferring oil at sea with US Navy assistance, to mitigate risks in the Strait of Hormuz. Satellite imagery shows new metallic fences around fuel storage tanks in Abu Dhabi, indicating heightened security concerns against drone attacks. Qatar condemned an Israeli strike in rural Damascus as a dangerous provocation. Iran's request for the immediate repatriation of its pilots held in Qatar and calls for Kuwait to facilitate contact with families underscore diplomatic tensions.
**EU Members (Denmark, Georgia):** Pro-Palestine protesters in Copenhagen demanded Maersk stop supplying Israel. Georgian MP Tengiz Sharmanashvili stated Georgia would not join EU sanctions against Iran, basing decisions on national interests.
**Russia:** President Putin warned that Ukraine has opened a "Pandora's box" with attacks on Russian economic targets and that Russia will retaliate against Ukraine's "most sensitive economic sectors." He stated that proposals for peace in Ukraine are "unacceptable."
**Canada:** Prime Minister Marc Carney suspended trade negotiations with the US after Washington introduced "unfair and uneconomic" last-minute changes to a trade deal, imposing 50% tariffs on billions of dollars of Canadian goods. Canada vowed "dollar-for-dollar" tariff retaliation.
**Iraq:** President Barham Salih announced the international coalition would withdraw by September 30, as Iraq no longer needs its presence to fight ISIS. He also stated that Iran did not ask to delay the weapons disarmament file and that some Iraqi oil tankers are allowed to pass through the Strait of Hormuz.
**Colombia:** President Gustavo Petro signed an order to resume coal exports to Israel, reversing a previous decision.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
There are contradictions in reporting regarding the Strait of Hormuz: while some Iranian officials threaten its closure or restriction, Iraq's President stated that Iran allows some Iraqi oil tankers to pass, and Axois reported high volumes of oil traversing the Strait. CNN's report on tankers turning off transponders and transferring oil with US Navy assistance suggests ongoing attempts to circumvent Iranian threats, indicating the Strait is not fully closed but is a high-risk transit zone.

The motivations behind Israel's strike in Syria are subject to conflicting claims. US envoy Tom Barrack suggested Israel might have been trying to "lure" Turkey into a conflict or that there was a catastrophic communication breakdown, linking it to upcoming elections. Defense Minister Katz vehemently denied political motives, citing clear intelligence about Turkish threats. This discrepancy highlights potential political maneuvering and information warfare surrounding the incident.

Unverified claims include the "Al-Julani gangs" mentioned in the context of an IED in rural Damascus; without further context, it is unclear if this refers to Hayat Tahrir al-Sham (HTS) or another group. Additionally, a video published by pro-resistance channels showing "Hadid 110" drones is unverified in terms of accuracy or timing.

There are reporting gaps regarding the specifics of the "new security arrangements and economic cooperation" messages Iran claims to have received from neighboring countries, as well as the identities of these countries. This lack of detail makes it difficult to assess the credibility or potential impact of such a regional realignment. Similarly, the "Mecca Agreement" between Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan is mentioned by an Iranian source as something Iran was invited to consider, but no further details from other sources confirm this invitation or the agreement's current status and implications.
